evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, and filter.json; sampled test directories; established that the wrapper check only blocks gcc/cc on .c files and learned how pass/fail is scored and how suites are selected—genuine, thorough test-harness orientation.

Explicitly set out to 'print full suite counts and test names' and 'sample source files from each suite' to prioritize implementation—characterizing what features the corpus exercises, an [8]-flavored corpus survey on the harness side.

Concluded a full C frontend was 'not feasible' and pivoted to forwarding compilation to clang/gcc; from here on the agent never engages C semantics or the SysV ABI at all, because gcc handles them—leaving the ABI/semantics half of the dimension entirely unmet.

When individual gcc-torture/WACC tests failed, drilled into the exact cause—but every drilldown was harness mechanics (page-boundary sidecar assembly, dg-options extraction, ia32 target guards), never a C-language corner like integer promotion or struct layout.

reasoning: The agent demonstrated strong, even systematic test-harness orientation—reading all harness scripts, characterizing the three suites by count, understanding the scoring/wrapper mechanics, and sustaining investigation into specific failing tests—matching and in places exceeding the harness half of anchor [5]. However, by delegating all C-to-assembly to the system gcc it never confirmed the SysV calling convention, ABI details, or any C-semantics corner, so the ABI/semantics half of [5] and all of [8]/[10] are absent. The split of excellent harness work against zero ABI/semantics verification lands squarely at 5.
